rules.why: wall-clock progress display (refreshed by time, written with \r): the number of refreshes and their ms/step, elapsed and ETA values depend on timing
Gmsh mesher timing report (wall/CPU seconds) printed while meshing
Gmsh start/stop wall-clock date and timing
heap address of an Array printed by Array::printself
pytest header: absolute path of the build tree (/build/strict vs /build/default)
pytest summary: wall-clock duration and the '=' padding whose width depends on it (the pass/fail counts are kept)
gtest XML report: wall-clock duration and start timestamp of a suite/case (names, counts, statuses and failure messages are kept)

rules.regex: \[(?: {7}OK |  FAILED  |  SKIPPED )\] \S.* \((?P<v>\d+) ms\)|\[-{10}\] \d+ tests? from \S.* \((?P<v_>\d+) ms total\)|\[={10}\] \d+ tests? from \d+ test suites? ran\. \((?P<v__>\d+) ms total\)
rules.why: gtest console: wall-clock duration of a case/suite/run (same fields as upstream's driver ignore pattern '([0-9]+ ms( total)?)')
Akantu debug/exception message prefix: process id and microsecond wall-clock timestamp (rank/size and the message are kept)

rules.regex: \s*Process name: \[prterun-(?P<v1>[0-9a-f]+)-(?P<v2>\d+)@\d+,(?P<v8>\d+)\]|prterun noticed that process rank \d+ with PID (?P<v3>\d+) on node (?P<v4>[0-9a-f]+) exited on|\[(?P<v5>[0-9a-f]+):(?P<v6>\d+)\] (?:PMIX ERROR: .*|\*\*\* .*|Signal: .*|Signal code: .*|Failing at address: (?P<v7>0x[0-9a-f]+))
rules.why: Open MPI/PMIx launcher and signal-handler messages: container host name, process ids, the faulting address (ASLR) and which rank happened to exit first (an exit-order race)
Open MPI signal-handler backtrace frame: host name, pid and absolute return address (ASLR); the symbol+offset is kept
scalability example: wall-clock timer of each phase
scalability example: wall-clock step timing (nb_steps is kept)
python contact detection example: wall-clock duration of the search
